fieldMarks: Stout toadlike amphibian to about 7 cm; light to dark brown, olive or blackish above, mottled with dark brown, with a yellow lyre-shaped pair of lines down the back.
Large protruding eyes with vertically elliptical pupils; no raised boss between the eyes.
Single sickle-shaped black spade on the inner side of each hind foot; skin with small warts and small parotoid glands.
Male call is a coarse nasal 'wank' or 'quonk' repeated every few seconds.
behavior: Nocturnal burrower that spends most of the time underground, becoming active on warm, damp or rainy nights.
Breeds whenever heavy rains fill temporary pools and temperatures exceed about 45 F; breeding groups may number dozens to hundreds; larvae can metamorphose in as little as 2 weeks.
Eats ants, beetles, flies, grasshoppers, crickets, termites and worms; skin secretions can irritate people, so wash hands after handling.
habitat: Sandy, gravelly or loose soils in wooded or open terrain, including sand prairies, pastures, farmland and suburbs; uses temporary rain-filled pools for breeding.
range: Eastern and southeastern United States from Massachusetts to Florida and west to the Mississippi River basin; absent from higher Appalachian elevations; not in Canada.

lookalikes.name: Plains spadefoot
lookalikes.howToTell: Has a raised boss between the eyes and a wedge-shaped spade at the base of each hind foot (Missouri Department of Conservation).
